**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, term-termination).**

What I found in Section 4 (¶p0024, ¶p0026):

1. **No Company convenience exit mid-term** — Section 4.1 gives a 1-year term with automatic annual renewal, terminable only "by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice," effectively tied to the renewal anniversary. Our playbook requires a 30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid fees.
2. **HDI has a mirror walk-away right** — the same 90-day notice reads as exercisable by HDI, potentially mid-term. Vendors should not be able to exit a committed term.
3. **Punitive exit fee** — Section 4.2(a) requires the Company to pay a Termination Payment of (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2, i.e. ~50% of annual Net Sales, where our fees under Section 3.1 are only 30% of Net Sales. That is many multiples of our 3-month fallback cap, and it applies even when we terminate because HDI failed to perform (including under Section 1.6).

Redline (validated, preferred level):
- ¶p0024: Company may terminate for convenience at any time on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees; HDI's convenience right limited to taking effect at the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.
- ¶p0026: Termination Payment capped at fees for the three months preceding the Termination Date, with no payment due where we terminate for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6.
